Q1.text: You have made us for Yourself, and our hearts are restless until they rest in You.
Q1.attribution: Augustine, Confessions I.1.1, translated by J. G. Pilkington, in Nicene and Post Nicene Fathers, first series, volume 1; New Advent edition. An invocation to God, not a promise that faith removes all anxiety.

Q2.text: the encounter with an event, a person
Q2.attribution: Benedict XVI, Deus caritas est 1, official English text. A short excerpt about the origin of Christian life.

Q3.text: in communion, in intimacy, with Jesus Christ
Q3.attribution: Saint John Paul II, Catechesi tradendae 5, official English text. A phrase identifying catechesis' aim.

Q4.text: For He was made man that we might be made God
Q4.attribution: Athanasius, On the Incarnation 54.3, translated by Archibald Robertson, Nicene and Post Nicene Fathers, second series, volume 4; New Advent edition. Explain participation by grace, not becoming another divine being or sharing God's essence by nature.

Q5.text: Through the Holy Spirit comes our restoration to paradise
Q5.attribution: Basil of Caesarea, On the Holy Spirit 15.36, translated by Blomfield Jackson, Nicene and Post Nicene Fathers, second series, volume 8; New Advent edition. Read as an account of the Spirit's saving gifts.

Q6.text: wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the Catholic Church
Q6.attribution: Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Smyrnaeans 8, translated by Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson, Ante Nicene Fathers, volume 1; New Advent edition. Early witness to Christ, Eucharist and episcopal communion; not a standalone proof of every later ecclesiological formulation.

Q7.text: The Pope is not an absolute monarch whose thoughts and desires are law.
Q7.attribution: Benedict XVI, homily at Saint John Lateran, 7 May 2005, official English text. Read with his explanation that teaching authority serves God's Word.

Q8.text: For me, prayer is a surge of the heart
Q8.attribution: Thérèse of Lisieux, Manuscript C 25r, as quoted in CCC 2558. The extract introduces a description embracing trial as well as joy.

Q9.text: the knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary
Q9.attribution: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.22.4, translated by Alexander Roberts and William Rambaut, Ante Nicene Fathers, volume 1; New Advent edition. Explain Mary's grace-enabled response in relation to Christ, not an independent source of redemption.

Q10.attribution: Teresa of Ávila, Life 8.5, as quoted in CCC 2709. A brief phrase from her account of prayer; not a test that every prayer must feel emotionally intimate.

Q11.text: Our prayer is public and common
Q11.attribution: Cyprian, On the Lord's Prayer 8, translated by Robert Ernest Wallis, Ante Nicene Fathers, volume 5; New Advent edition. The context explains why Jesus teaches “our,” rather than only individual petitions.

Q12.text: seeing is far more persuasive than hearing
Q12.attribution: Mystagogical Catechesis I.1, transmitted under Cyril of Jerusalem; Catechetical Lecture 19 in the linked edition, translated by Edwin Hamilton Gifford, Nicene and Post Nicene Fathers, second series, volume 7. Attribution of the mystagogical lectures is discussed by scholars; identify the textual tradition rather than claiming certainty beyond it. The original addresses the newly baptised.

Q13.text: For not as common bread and common drink do we receive these
Q13.attribution: Justin Martyr, First Apology 66, translated by Marcus Dods and George Reith, Ante Nicene Fathers, volume 1; New Advent edition. Read alongside his account of Christ's flesh and blood and Sunday worship in chapters 65–67.

Q14.text: Jesus Christ is the face of the Father's mercy.
Q14.attribution: Francis, Misericordiae vultus 1, official English text; apostrophe normalised typographically. The course draws from the document, not from a prediction of any individual's spiritual or medical outcome.

Q15.attribution: Saint Leo the Great, Sermon 21.3, as quoted in CCC 1691. Read with the baptismal summons to live accordingly.
